Peer result also includes C24, C26, C42, C43 which OpenEval addresses separately.

Both find these claims supported, with OpenEval providing specific figure references and peer reviewers noting convincing evidence.

Perfect alignment on C20-C23. Both agree the inverse relationship between gain and stability in feedforward circuits is well-supported. OpenEval cites Figure 3-4 and mathematical framework, while peer reviewer notes this as a major strength with thorough investigation.

Perfect alignment on C27, C28, C59. Both explicitly praise the noise simulation validation (Figure 6) that extends findings beyond linearization. Peer reviewers particularly emphasize this addresses limitations of fixed-point analysis for understanding in vivo dynamics.

Perfect alignment on C32, C33, C57 regarding tuning curve analysis. Both find the systematic characterization across network configurations supported. Peer reviewers acknowledge the link to visual processing computations and experimental literature bridge.

Perfect alignment on C11-C13. Both agree these cited experimental findings about opposite SOM modulation effects are accurate and appropriately used to motivate the theoretical investigation. No challenges to the experimental citations.

Strong overlap on C29-C31, C41, C53 regarding synaptic weight effects on gain and stability. Both find the systematic analysis in Figure 7 well-supported. Peer reviewer highlights this thorough investigation as a major strength. OpenEval also includes C53 not mentioned in peer result.

Partial overlap on C44, C45 regarding rate-dependent gain effects. OpenEval finds these supported by Figures 3-5 with appropriate experimental citations. Peer R10 finds this observation consistent with model analysis and experimental work, noting it bridges to experimental literature.

Both address biological interpretations (C34-C37). OpenEval finds the logic connecting circuit structure to function compelling but notes inference beyond direct evidence. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of direct biological comparison despite not directly challenging the claims.

Partial overlap on model architecture (C14, C15). OpenEval finds mathematical derivation clearly demonstrates the framework. Peer reviewers praise the model design balance between biological detail and mathematical tractability. Both find model assumptions well-justified.

Both address foundational background claims (C1-C3). OpenEval notes these are well-supported by extensive citations providing context. Peer reviewers confirm these well-established background claims, with Reviewer 1 acknowledging the foundational premise about inhibitory pathways.

Strong overlap on historical/functional context (C6-C10). OpenEval finds all claims well-supported by appropriate citations establishing background. Peer reviewers agree these are well-established background claims, with no challenges to the foundational statements.

Both address linearization limitation (C58, C59). OpenEval acknowledges linearization as limitation but notes C59 shows results hold with noise. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge both the limitation and its mitigation through simulations, suggesting future work in chaotic/oscillatory regimes.

Partial overlap on experimental citations (C46, C47). OpenEval finds these well-supported by experimental literature. Peer R9 includes these in biological interpretation evaluation rated UNCERTAIN, suggesting insufficient direct biological comparison despite not refuting the claims.
